name: Marching Tetrahedra and Decomposition
text:
# Marching Tetrahedra and Decomposition

Also called: Tetrahedral Marching, MC-Tet

## Overview
Marching Tetrahedra and Decomposition is an [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) method that resolves the topological ambiguities inherent in standard Marching Cubes by decomposing each cubic voxel into a fixed set of tetrahedra [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md]. Unlike Marching Cubes, which requires complex disambiguation logic for ambiguous cases, this method ensures a unique intersection topology for each of the 16 possible vertex configurations within a tetrahedron [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md]. It sets itself apart from its siblings by replacing the finite [lookup table of configurations](#4978-lookup-table-and-configuration.md) with a deterministic algorithm that reconstructs a local polygonal approximation given any number of intersections, and from [Error Analysis via Marching Tetrahedra](1308-error-analysis-via-marching-tetrahedra.md) by focusing on topological correctness and feature resolution rather than error bounds [1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a [regular grid](#3950-regular-grid.md) (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers. The core mechanism involves traversing the grid cells and evaluating the data to determine which parts of the domain constitute the surface [G].

1.  **Domain Traversal**: The algorithm iterates over the volume data structure [G]. For regular grids, this often involves checking each cell or voxel [G].
2.  **Surface Determination**: A criterion is applied to identify surface locations. In isosurface methods, this involves comparing scalar values against a threshold (isovalue) to detect sign changes or equality [30-isosurface-extraction.md]. In [blocky meshing](#31-blocky-meshing.md), this involves checking occupancy states or material IDs to identify exposed boundaries [31-blocky-meshing.md].
3.  **Primitive Generation**: Geometric primitives (vertices, edges, faces) are generated based on the determined surface locations [G].
4.  **Mesh Coherence**: Adjacent primitives are merged or connected to form a coherent mesh, often requiring vertex merging to avoid duplicates and ensure watertightness [30-isosurface-extraction.md].

## Subtopics

### [Error Analysis via Marching Tetrahedra](1308-error-analysis-via-marching-tetrahedra.md)
A metric for evaluating the geometric and topological approximation error when fusing two child tetrahedra into a single parent tetrahedron within a [multiresolution tetrahedral framework](#1183-multi-tetra-framework.md) [1308-error-analysis-via-marching-tetrahedra.md]. It determines whether the simplification of the mesh preserves the isosurface geometry defined by a specific threshold [1308-error-analysis-via-marching-tetrahedra.md]. Unlike sibling methods that may rely on view-dependent projection or generic distance bounds, this method explicitly calculates the physical displacement of isosurface intersection points along specific segments within the tetrahedron, ensuring topological consistency during fusion [1308-error-analysis-via-marching-tetrahedra.md].

### [Subgrid Marching Tetrahedra](1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md)
A method for recovering a manifold, intersection-free triangle mesh from the points where edges of a tetrahedral grid pierce a continuous surface [1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md]. It allows arbitrarily many surface patches within a single cell, capturing fine features and thin sheets, without requiring a well-defined inside/outside or consistently-oriented input geometry [1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md]. Unlike [classic](#5024-classic-column-voxel-space.md) marching cubes or tets, which are limited to at most one intersection per edge, this scheme defines connectivity for arbitrary patterns of edge intersections [1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md]. It sets itself apart from its parent [Marching Tetrahedra and Decomposition](11174-marching-tetrahedra-and-decomposition.md) by replacing the finite lookup table of configurations with a deterministic algorithm that reconstructs a local polygonal approximation given any number of intersections, and from [Error Analysis via Marching Tetrahedra](1308-error-analysis-via-marching-tetrahedra.md) by focusing on topological correctness and feature resolution rather than error bounds [1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md].

### [Marching Cubes Tetrahedron Decomposition](9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md)
A [surface extraction](#29-surface-extraction.md) algorithm that resolves the topological ambiguities inherent in standard Marching Cubes by decomposing each cubic voxel into a fixed set of tetrahedra [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md]. Unlike Marching Cubes, which requires complex disambiguation logic for ambiguous cases, this method ensures a unique intersection topology for each of the 16 possible vertex configurations within a tetrahedron [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md].

## Background
The method originates from the need to resolve the topological ambiguities present in the original Marching Cubes algorithm, which could produce non-manifold geometries in specific ambiguous cases [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md]. By decomposing the cube into tetrahedra, the problem is reduced to the 16 unambiguous cases of a tetrahedron [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md]. It is widely used in medical imaging and scientific visualization where topological correctness is critical [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md].
